concerns.text: Tasks T034.1 and T034 implement a fallback to Wilcoxon triggered by 'convergence failure' detection. However, FR-006 explicitly mandates the fallback trigger be 'Shapiro-Wilk p < 0.05'. The tasks silently replace the spec's required statistical trigger with an undefined 'convergence failure' logic, violating the requirement to use Shapiro-Wilk as the switch condition.

FR-009 requires a 'pre-study pilot check (n=5)' to validate SART/Ospan functionality. Tasks T014.1 and T019.1 describe simulating this locally via a 'static bundle' and 'local web interface wrapper'. This silently relaxes the requirement for 'real-call testing' (FR-007 context) and 'pilot check' by substiting a synthetic simulation, which does not satisfy the empirical validation of the actual web interface logic against real user interaction or the OSF reference as implied by the spec's intent for a pilot.

FR-011 requires generating a sensitivity analysis report 'comparing self-reported compliance logs against objective screen-time data (if available)'. Task T038 only implements logic to 'document limitations if no objective data exists'. It fails to implement the 'compare' clause of the requirement, silently dropping the acceptance criterion for handling the case where objective data IS available.

FR-002 mandates administering tasks via a web interface using 'standard scoring algorithms defined in the OSF task repository (v2.1+)'. Task T011.1 only generates a 'static web interface bundle' and T014.1 simulates interaction. There is no task to verify the bundle actually implements the OSF v2.1+ logic or to integrate the reference code, silently weakening the requirement to use the specific OSF reference implementation.
